description: Fundamental concepts in chemistry including atomic structure, bonding, and reactions

atomic_structure.protons: Positively charged particles in the nucleus; define the element
atomic_structure.neutrons: Neutral particles in the nucleus; define isotopes
atomic_structure.electrons: Negatively charged particles in orbitals around the nucleus
atomic_structure.atomic_number: Number of protons in an atom
atomic_structure.atomic_mass: Average mass of an element's isotopes, measured in atomic mass units (amu)

periodic_table.groups: Vertical columns; elements share similar chemical properties
periodic_table.periods: Horizontal rows; elements share the same number of electron shells

notable_groups.alkali_metals: Group 1; highly reactive, one valence electron
notable_groups.halogens: Group 17; highly reactive nonmetals, form salts with metals

chemical_bonding.ionic: Transfer of electrons between atoms; forms oppositely charged ions
chemical_bonding.covalent: Sharing of electrons between atoms; can be single, double, or triple bonds
chemical_bonding.metallic: Electrons delocalized across a lattice of metal ions
chemical_bonding.hydrogen_bonding: Weak attractive force between hydrogen and electronegative atoms (N, O, F)

states_of_matter.solid: Fixed shape and volume; particles vibrate in fixed positions
states_of_matter.liquid: Fixed volume, variable shape; particles flow past each other
states_of_matter.gas: Variable shape and volume; particles move freely
states_of_matter.plasma: Ionized gas; fourth state found in stars and fluorescent lights

types_of_reactions.synthesis: A + B → AB; two substances combine to form one
types_of_reactions.decomposition: AB → A + B; one compound breaks into simpler substances
types_of_reactions.single_replacement: A + BC → AC + B; one element replaces another in a compound
types_of_reactions.double_replacement: AB + CD → AD + CB; ions exchange between two compounds

ph_scale.acidic: pH < 7; excess H⁺ ions (e.g., HCl, vinegar)
ph_scale.basic_alkaline: pH > 7; excess OH⁻ ions (e.g., NaOH, baking soda)

hydrocarbons.alkanes: Single bonds only (e.g., methane CH₄, ethane C₂H₆)
hydrocarbons.alkenes: At least one double bond (e.g., ethene C₂H₄)
hydrocarbons.alkynes: At least one triple bond (e.g., ethyne C₂H₂)
hydrocarbons.aromatics: Ring structures with delocalized electrons (e.g., benzene C₆H₆)
